requirements.requirement: The system must call the provider triage API when a provider result is selected or displayed in the chat flow.
The system must map API response fields to the frontend triage display schema defined in EVAL-P-TRIAGE-UX-S1.
The system must render triage UI components from EVAL-P-TRIAGE-UX-S3 using the mapped data without runtime errors.
The system must display a loading state within the chat UI while the triage API request is in progress.
The system must replace the loading state with triage results immediately upon successful API response.
The system must preserve message ordering in the chat flow when inserting triage results.
The system must display an error state in the chat UI if the triage API request fails (e.g., network or server error).
The system must allow the user to retry the triage request after an error state is shown.
The system must display an empty state when the API returns no triage data for a provider.
The system must not crash or render undefined values when partial triage data is returned.
The system must ensure specialty match reasoning is displayed before any quality-related reasoning in the rendered output.
The system must correctly render pass/fail status based on the API response without inversion or ambiguity.
The system must sanitize and safely render any text content returned from the triage API to prevent injection or malformed UI.
The system must log triage API request failures and mapping errors to the frontend error monitoring system.
The system must not issue duplicate triage API requests for the same provider within a single chat session unless explicitly retried.
The system must maintain consistency between the triage API contract and frontend schema, failing gracefully if schema mismatch occurs.
The system must render triage results within the existing ChatWindow component without breaking existing message rendering behavior.
The system must ensure that LLM-generated explanatory text (if present in API response) is displayed exactly as returned without reordering or truncation.
The system must not hallucinate or fabricate triage reasoning content beyond what is provided by the API response.
The system must preserve semantic grouping of reasoning blocks (e.g., specialty vs quality) as provided by the API response.
